assessment_prompts.independence: Can you teach coach the coach to others and build systems so it keeps running?

4|Coaching to Protect Long-Term Quality.trainee_content:
Coach the cause and USP of each campaign, and use the quality data to pick your coaching priorities early — before problems show up in the numbers, not after.

Help BAs see why quality matters to their own earnings and the office's future. Then follow up until the change in behaviour sticks.
what_good_looks_like: Coaches quality from data trends, not single incidents
BAs can explain why quality matters, not just say the rules
Follows up after coaching to check the change held
how_measured: Quality KPIs (1st/3rd payment, cancellations) hold steady or go up
Coaching priorities clearly come from the data, before problems hit
Spot-checks show coached behaviours still in place weeks later
leader_coaching_notes: Ask: what does the quality data say your top three coaching priorities are?
Watch one quality coaching conversation start to finish
Check follow-up: pick one past fix and see if it stuck

assessment_prompts.knowledge: Can you explain how you coach to protect long-term quality and why it matters at this level?
assessment_prompts.skill: Show me a quality coaching conversation, live, with your team watching.
assessment_prompts.consistency: Is your quality coaching hitting the standard week after week?
assessment_prompts.independence: Can you teach this to other leaders and build systems that protect quality without you?

4|Emotional Regulation While Coaching.trainee_content:
Separate the person from the performance problem. Don't get defensive when someone pushes back, and reset fast after a hard coaching conversation.

Stay steady. Your team should never have to guess what mood you're in before they bring you a problem.
what_good_looks_like: Same steady presence on the worst day as the best day
Takes challenge without getting defensive
Resets fast after hard talks — the next person gets a clean slate
how_measured: Team members bring problems early instead of hiding them
Coaching stays calm under pushback when watched
No 'check the mood first' habit on the team
leader_coaching_notes: Debrief their hardest recent conversation — what did they feel vs. show?
Watch for leaks: sarcasm, sighs, cold shoulders after a miss
Call out composure by name when you see it under real pressure

assessment_prompts.knowledge: Can you explain what emotional regulation while coaching means and why it matters at this level?
assessment_prompts.skill: Show me you staying steady in a hard coaching moment, live, with your team watching.
assessment_prompts.consistency: Do you stay steady while coaching, week after week?
assessment_prompts.independence: Can you teach this steadiness to other leaders and build it into how the team runs?

4|Environment & Culture.trainee_content:
Spot when culture and atmosphere are hurting retention or results, and act on it.

Build and protect a place where positive energy and high standards make people want to stay — a team that's fun and professional at the same time, and strong enough that it doesn't rest on the owner alone.
what_good_looks_like: Reads the room and acts on culture problems early
Standards and fun live together — neither gets dropped for the other
Culture holds when they're away — it lives in the team, not one person
how_measured: Retention numbers in their team
New starters describe the team the way you'd want them to
Culture survives their holiday
leader_coaching_notes: Ask what the culture problem is right now — there always is one
Watch a morning meeting for the energy vs. discipline balance
Check whose energy the room depends on — it shouldn't be one person's

assessment_prompts.knowledge: Can you explain what environment and culture mean here and why they matter at this level?
assessment_prompts.skill: Show me you building or fixing culture, live, with your team watching.
assessment_prompts.consistency: Does your team's culture hold to the standard week after week?
assessment_prompts.independence: Can you teach culture-building to others and make it run without you?

4|Handling Conflict & Underperformance.trainee_content:
Don't dodge conflict and don't let it drag. And don't mix up being fair with keeping everyone happy.

When someone underperforms, deal with it fast and fair: clear expectations, a real chance to improve, then a decision. Once it's resolved, the team moves on.
what_good_looks_like: Deals with issues within days, not weeks
Fair process: clear expectation, support, deadline, decision
Once resolved, it's resolved — no grudges or replays
how_measured: Written, time-bound plans exist for repeated underperformance
Conflicts end with both a decision and a working relationship
Team surveys and retention show no issues left to rot
leader_coaching_notes: Review their open underperformance cases — does each one have a deadline?
Roleplay the conversation they are avoiding
Check the aftermath of past conflicts: resolved or just quiet?

assessment_prompts.knowledge: Can you explain how you handle conflict and underperformance and why it matters at this level?
assessment_prompts.skill: Show me you handling a real underperformance conversation, live, with your team watching.
assessment_prompts.consistency: Do you handle conflict and underperformance to the standard week after week?
assessment_prompts.independence: Can you teach this to other leaders and build a process so it happens without you?

4|Mentoring Through Business Cycles.trainee_content:
The business moves in cycles. Recruitment pushes, slow seasons, campaign changes. Highs and lows are normal.

Your role is to coach people through them. Keep them focused on what they can control and the right actions, whether things are up or down.

Each cycle should teach your people something. After a slow season, they should be better at handling the next one on their own. That is how experience turns into judgement.
what_good_looks_like: Treats cycles as normal. No panic in dips, no coasting in peaks
Coaches what people control: activity, quality, attitude
After each cycle, the person can handle more on their own
how_measured: Team results stay steady through seasonal swings
People bring up past cycles when facing new ones
People stay through the down periods
leader_coaching_notes: In a dip, check what they coach: effort and inputs, or just mood?
Have them write the plan for the next slow season
After every cycle, ask: what will your people do alone next time?

assessment_prompts.knowledge: Can you explain how to mentor people through business cycles, and why it matters at this level?
assessment_prompts.skill: Can you show me how you coach someone through a cycle, live, with your team watching?
assessment_prompts.consistency: Do you coach people through cycles to the standard, week after week?
assessment_prompts.independence: Can you teach this to others and build systems so it happens without you?

4|Predicting Issues Early.trainee_content:
One bad day is noise. Three bad days might be a pattern. You need to know the difference.

At this level you spot problems before they cost you a week. The numbers warn you early, and you act early.

Use tools like AI and automation to catch what you would miss checking by hand. Let the tools widen what you can see.
what_good_looks_like: Tells noise from real signal in the numbers
Acts on patterns before they turn into bad results
Uses tools to see more than a manual check would
how_measured: Steps in before the visible drop, not after
Has made predictions that came true
Has set up automated checks or reports
leader_coaching_notes: Ask for one prediction a week. Review the hit rate together
After any surprise, dig in: what pattern was visible in hindsight?
Bring in one new tool or report per quarter and check they use it

assessment_prompts.knowledge: Can you explain how to spot issues early, and why it matters at this level?
assessment_prompts.skill: Can you show me, live with your team watching, how you catch a problem early?
assessment_prompts.consistency: Do you catch issues early to the standard, week after week?
assessment_prompts.independence: Can you teach this to others and build systems that catch issues without you?

4|Preventing Dependency.trainee_content:
If your people can't move without checking with you first, you haven't built leaders. You've built dependence.

Build independence on purpose. Coach in a way that grows their ability, not their reliance on you. As they get stronger, pull the support back, step by step.

The end goal: you have truly replaced yourself.
what_good_looks_like: Answers with a question when the person should know the answer
Support is scaffolding. It comes down on a schedule
People stop asking permission for calls that are theirs to make
how_measured: Fewer things get escalated to them, month over month
Their people make the right call without checking first
A full day runs without anyone needing them
leader_coaching_notes: Count their interruptions for a day. Each one is a dependency signal
Coach the phrase: 'What do you think, and what would you do?'
Each month, review which supports can come down

assessment_prompts.knowledge: Can you explain what dependency looks like and why preventing it matters at this level?
assessment_prompts.skill: Can you show me, live with your team watching, how you build independence instead of reliance?
assessment_prompts.consistency: Do you build independence in your people, week after week?
assessment_prompts.independence: Can you teach this to others and build systems so independence grows without you?

4|Profitability vs. Spending.trainee_content:
Know the key numbers that decide whether the office makes money. Cold.

Budget and plan ahead. Don't wait for a shortfall and react.

Spend on purpose. Put money into people, into development and growth, where it pays back and keeps paying back. Cut spending where it doesn't. Profit funds the mission. Treat it that way.
what_good_looks_like: Knows the office's break-even and what drives margin, cold
Budgets ahead instead of reacting to shortfalls
Spends on development and growth, not out of habit
how_measured: Can walk through the office profit numbers without prompting
Spending plans exist before the money moves
Money spent shows a return in people or performance
leader_coaching_notes: Quiz the numbers monthly: break-even, cost per recruit, margin per BA
Pick one recent spend: what return did they expect, and did it land?
Coach the balance. Underspending on people is also a failure

assessment_prompts.knowledge: Can you explain how profit and spending work in this office, and why it matters at this level?
assessment_prompts.skill: Can you walk me through a real spending call, live, with your team watching?
assessment_prompts.consistency: Do you budget and spend to the standard, week after week?
assessment_prompts.independence: Can you teach this to others and build systems so the money side runs without you?

4|Scaling Beyond Personal Production.trainee_content:
At this stage you no longer carry the team's numbers yourself. You've moved from making results to building people who make results.

Hand over real responsibility. Don't become the bottleneck everything runs through.

Your output is now what your people deliver. The proof: the whole thing keeps working when you step out.
what_good_looks_like: Hands over real responsibility, not just tasks
Team results hold up when they step out of production
Builds capacity before it's needed, not while firefighting
how_measured: Team total holds on days they don't personally sell
Every key responsibility has a named owner
A full day runs start to finish without them there
leader_coaching_notes: Check the delegation map. Who owns what, and do they know it?
Plan a step-back day on purpose and review what wobbled
Coach them off any task only they can do. That's the bottleneck

assessment_prompts.knowledge: Can you explain what scaling beyond your own production means, and why it matters at this level?
assessment_prompts.skill: Can you show me, live with your team watching, how you hand over real responsibility?
assessment_prompts.consistency: Does your team deliver without you carrying the numbers, week after week?
assessment_prompts.independence: Can you teach this to others and build a structure that runs without you?

4|Stage 4 \u2014 The Team Builder Standa.trainee_content:
Stage 4 is about building systems, setting standards, and creating independence. You stop being the one who produces results and become the one who builds people who produce results.

Everything at this stage comes down to one question: does your team run to the standard when you are not in the room?

Talk is not enough. Every standard must have a number attached and a consequence when it's missed.
what_good_looks_like: Evidence: accurate team data, captured every time
Evidence: a full day runs start to finish without you there
Evidence: people move backward when performance drops. The ladder works both ways
Evidence: quality risks get spotted early, with a coaching fix attached
Evidence: people keep moving up into leadership. The pipeline keeps producing
how_measured: Keeps every Stage 3 standard running and builds on it
Repeated underperformance gets a written, time-bound action
Repeated misses pause progression
Own profit and quality standards hold while building others
leader_coaching_notes: Review this standard at the start of every Stage 4 coaching cycle
Ask for the evidence, not the story. Each item above is checkable
If a standard has no number and no consequence, it isn't a standard yet

assessment_prompts.knowledge: Can you explain the Team Builder Standard and why it matters at this level?
assessment_prompts.skill: Can you show me the standard working, live, with your team watching?
assessment_prompts.consistency: Does your team hit this standard week after week, even when you're not there?
assessment_prompts.independence: Can you teach the standard to others and build systems that hold it without you?

4|Teaching Advanced Sign-Up Psychology.trainee_content:
At Stage 4 you teach the psychology behind how people decide. Why people say yes. What builds trust in seconds. How urgency works without pressure.

Then you coach your BAs to use it in a way that's natural, ethical, and works.

This is next-level sign-up skill. It's not you running the 5 Steps yourself anymore. It's making the thinking behind them something you can pass on.
what_good_looks_like: Teaches the why behind each step, not just the what
BAs they coach use the psychology naturally. It never sounds scripted
Keeps it ethical: the supporter feels good about saying yes
how_measured: A BA they coached can explain the psychology back correctly
Watch a roleplay: their teaching shows up in the BA's next live pitch
Quality numbers hold or rise as skills advance
leader_coaching_notes: Have them teach one psychology principle in a huddle and watch the room
Check a week later: did the coached BA keep the behaviour?
Correct any drift towards pressure tactics right away

assessment_prompts.knowledge: Can you explain the psychology behind why people say yes, and why teaching it matters at this level?
assessment_prompts.skill: Can you teach a piece of this psychology live, with your team watching?
assessment_prompts.consistency: Do you teach this to the standard, week after week?
assessment_prompts.independence: Can your BAs teach it to others, with systems that keep it going without you?

4|Tracking Progression & Retention.trainee_content:
Keep your team's reporting right, every time. Don't just count heads — track how each person moves through the stages.

You should know exactly when and where people drop out. And you hold your leaders to it: they answer for whether their people move up and stick around, not just for headcount.
what_good_looks_like: Knows exactly who is at which stage and who is stuck
Spots where people drop out and fixes the stage, not the person
Leaders answer for their people's growth, not just their sales
how_measured: Stage-by-stage progression report exists and is up to date
Drop-off review with clear actions attached
Retention and move-up rates tracked by leader
leader_coaching_notes: Look at the progression board every week — every stuck name needs a plan
Put leaders' retention side by side and coach the gap
Praise move-ups in front of everyone — what gets tracked and praised repeats

assessment_prompts.knowledge: Can you explain how you track progression and retention, and why it matters at this level?
assessment_prompts.skill: Show me how you track progression and retention, live, with your team watching.
assessment_prompts.consistency: Do you run this tracking to the standard week after week?
assessment_prompts.independence: Have you taught this to others and built a system so it runs without you?

4|Using KPIs to Coach.trainee_content:
The numbers tell you what's really wrong — learn to find the root cause, not the symptom. Then teach your leaders to read and use their own KPIs the same way.

Data is your coaching language. Every coaching move starts with what the numbers say, and ends with the change you expect to see in them.
what_good_looks_like: Reads a KPI sheet and lands on the real cause, not the symptom
Their leaders can read their own numbers and spot their own problems
Every coaching action has a number attached to it
how_measured: Leaders can walk through their own KPIs without help
Coaching actions name specific numbers and the change expected
Root-cause calls turn out right over the following weeks
leader_coaching_notes: Hand them a KPI sheet cold and ask for the story in it
Check their leaders: who can self-diagnose, who still needs the answer?
Follow one coaching move: number before, action, number after

assessment_prompts.knowledge: Can you explain how you use KPIs to coach, and why it matters at this level?
assessment_prompts.skill: Show me how you coach from KPIs, live, with your team watching.
assessment_prompts.consistency: Do you coach from the numbers to the standard week after week?
assessment_prompts.independence: Have you taught this to others and built a system around it?

5|Accurate Sector Reporting.trainee_content:
Hold your sector to accurate Field IQ data — every field, every day, no shortcuts.

Track your territory data across the week so your impacts, prime-time roleplay, and coaching hit the real problems.

Bad data doesn't just fool you. It wastes everyone's coaching time.
what_good_looks_like: Sector's Field IQ is complete and correct every day
Chases gaps the same day, coaches repeat offenders
The week's territory picture drives the coaching calendar
how_measured: Data check: no missing fields across the sector
Coaching topics clearly come from the week's data
Zero fights over the numbers — everyone trusts them
leader_coaching_notes: Spot-check their sector's data every week
Check the chain: this week's data feeds next week's impacts
Coach them to make accuracy the sector's normal, not a nag

assessment_prompts.knowledge: Can you explain accurate sector reporting and why it matters at this level?
assessment_prompts.skill: Show me your sector reporting, live, with your team watching.
assessment_prompts.consistency: Is your sector's data right to the standard week after week?
assessment_prompts.independence: Have you taught this to others and built a system so it stays accurate without you?

5|Building Belief, Energy & Belonging.trainee_content:
Call out progress and small wins — not just sign-ups. Build relationships past your own team.

Know when morale or belief is slipping, and step in early, before it spreads.

A sector runs on belief as much as skill. Belief doesn't happen by accident — you build it on purpose.
what_good_looks_like: Celebrates progress and effort, not only results
Spots morale drops early and acts before they spread
Everyone in the sector feels seen — including the quiet ones
how_measured: Recognition moments happen every day, visibly
Steps in on morale early, before performance dropped
Sector retention and energy
leader_coaching_notes: Count praise vs. correction for one day — check the ratio
Ask who's struggling that the numbers don't show yet
Watch how the room responds when they walk in

assessment_prompts.knowledge: Can you explain how you build belief, energy and belonging, and why it matters at this level?
assessment_prompts.skill: Show me how you build belief and energy, live, with your team watching.
assessment_prompts.consistency: Does your sector feel that belief and energy from you week after week?
assessment_prompts.independence: Have you taught this to others and built it into how the sector runs?

5|Diagnosing Where BAs Lose Sign-Ups.trainee_content:
When a BA in your sector is losing sign-ups, you can name exactly which of the 5 or 8 Steps is leaking.

Watch them. Pinpoint the gap. Retrain that one skill — not the whole pitch. Then check the next set of numbers to prove the fix worked.
what_good_looks_like: Names the exact step where each struggling BA leaks
Retrains the specific gap, not the whole pitch
Proves the fix in the results, not in vibes
how_measured: Diagnosis, retrain, and measurable recovery — all on record
What they see in the field matches what the data says
Retrains are short and hit one target
leader_coaching_notes: Have them diagnose one BA by watching, then check it against the numbers
Watch one retrain: is it the step, or everything?
Track how long it takes from diagnosis to result

assessment_prompts.knowledge: Can you explain how you find where a BA is losing sign-ups, and why it matters at this level?
assessment_prompts.skill: Show me a live diagnosis and retrain, with your team watching.
assessment_prompts.consistency: Do you diagnose and fix to the standard week after week?
assessment_prompts.independence: Have you taught others to diagnose this way and built a system around it?

5|Emotional Control When Results Are Dow.trainee_content:
When results are down, the sector watches you. Stay in control in front of them.

Create urgency without fear or negativity. Call out poor performance without souring the room.

Your own frustration is yours to carry — the team gets what they need from you, not what you're feeling.
what_good_looks_like: Down days get urgency and belief, not blame and gloom
Calls out poor performance while keeping the room positive
The team can't read panic off them, ever
how_measured: Team energy holds through bad days
Watched on a down day: stays calm and helpful
No fear behaviour: hiding numbers, dodging the sector leader
leader_coaching_notes: Watch them on a bad day — that's the real test
Debrief after: what did you feel vs. what did you show?
Roleplay creating urgency without threat

assessment_prompts.knowledge: Can you explain emotional control when results are down, and why it matters at this level?
assessment_prompts.skill: Show me how you lead a down day, live, with your team watching.
assessment_prompts.consistency: Do you hold that control week after week, on the bad weeks too?
assessment_prompts.independence: Have you taught your leaders to lead down days the same way?

5|End-of-Day Sector Breakdown.trainee_content:
Run a proper end-of-day breakdown, every day. Every BA leaves knowing their plan for tomorrow.

Go through what the numbers said, what caused them, and exactly what each person works on next.

The breakdown is where today's results turn into tomorrow's coaching.
what_good_looks_like: Goes through numbers person by person, cause by cause
Every BA leaves with one specific thing to improve tomorrow
There for it every working day — no exceptions
how_measured: Breakdown happens every day, on record
Each BA has a next-day focus, and it gets followed up
Averages climb as the daily coaching stacks up
leader_coaching_notes: Sit in on one breakdown a month
Next morning, ask a BA what their focus is — it should match
Check the loop: yesterday's focus comes up in today's breakdown

assessment_prompts.knowledge: Can you explain the end-of-day breakdown and why it matters at this level?
assessment_prompts.skill: Run a breakdown for me, live, with your team there.

assessment_prompts.independence: Have you taught others to run it and built it into the sector's routine?

5|Full Ownership of Sector Results.trainee_content:
Your sector's number is your number. Own it fully.

When a week goes bad, don't just report it. Find the real reason it happened. No excuses about the territory, the weather, or the team you were given.

Own the miss, find the cause, and bring the fix.
what_good_looks_like: Talks in causes and fixes, never in blame
Digs past the first excuse to the real reason
Owns the miss out loud and owns the plan to fix it
how_measured: Finds the root cause of any down week and brings actions
Fixes hit the real cause and results come back
Never deflects in reviews
leader_coaching_notes: Push past their first answer: 'and what caused that?'
Check their diagnosis against the data yourself
Praise ownership loudly — that's the culture you're building

assessment_prompts.knowledge: Can you explain what full ownership of sector results means and why it matters at this level?
assessment_prompts.skill: Show me full ownership of sector results live, with your team watching.
assessment_prompts.consistency: Do you own your sector's results to the standard every week?
assessment_prompts.independence: Can you teach full ownership of sector results to others and build systems around it?

5|High-Level Planning & Organization.trainee_content:
Plan your impacts around your team and your territory. Have the week set before Monday — impacts, rotations, focus skills.

Then stay flexible. If the day calls for a specific coaching move, pivot. The plan serves the sector, not the other way around.
what_good_looks_like: Weekly plan done before Monday: impacts, patches, priorities
Pivots fast when the day needs it, without losing the week
Impacts fit specific people and territory, not generic
how_measured: Written weekly plan, checked against what actually happened
Daily pivots that fixed real needs
Impact sessions hit the right BA at the right time
leader_coaching_notes: Review their week plan every Monday for two months
Check one pivot: was it panic, or a real read of the day?
Coach impact specificity — 'who is this for and what changes?'

assessment_prompts.knowledge: Can you explain high-level planning and organisation and why it matters at this level?
assessment_prompts.skill: Show me high-level planning and organisation live, with your team watching.
assessment_prompts.consistency: Do you plan and organise to the standard every week?
assessment_prompts.independence: Can you teach planning and organisation to others and build systems around it?

5|Identifying & Correcting Quality.trainee_content:
Spot quality and conduct problems in your sector and fix them fast.

A quality problem caught at the doorstep costs one conversation. Caught at cancellation, it costs everyone.

Watch for the early signs and retrain the same day.
what_good_looks_like: Spots quality slipping in the field, not in next week's report
Corrects conduct problems right away, face to face
Retrains same day; escalates when the fix doesn't stick
how_measured: Sector quality KPIs (donations, cancellations) stay on standard
Same-day retrain record for problems found
No conduct problems surfacing later that they should have caught
leader_coaching_notes: Ask for the last quality problem they caught and what they did
Cross-check their sector's quality data against what they report
Roleplay the conduct conversation they least want to have

assessment_prompts.knowledge: Can you explain how to spot and fix quality problems, and why it matters at this level?
assessment_prompts.skill: Show me how you spot and fix a quality problem live, with your team watching.
assessment_prompts.consistency: Do you catch and fix quality problems to the standard every week?
assessment_prompts.independence: Can you teach others to spot and fix quality, and build systems around it?

5|Leading the Situation.trainee_content:
Nobody tells a sector leader where to look. You set your own priorities from what the sector and the team need.

The numbers and the field tell you where the problem is. Spot ratios slipping before they turn into bad results, and act first.
what_good_looks_like: Picks the right priority every day without being asked
Catches ratios slipping early and steps in
Owner never has to point them at the problem
how_measured: Priority calls they made before anyone asked
Ratio fixes dated before the results dipped
Owner step-ins at zero for the week
leader_coaching_notes: Morning check: what's your priority today and why?
Review one early catch and one they missed — what was visible?
If you had to direct them this week, coach that gap first

assessment_prompts.knowledge: Can you explain what leading the situation means and why it matters at this level?
assessment_prompts.skill: Show me leading the situation live, with your team watching.
assessment_prompts.consistency: Do you lead the situation to the standard every week?
assessment_prompts.independence: Can you teach leading the situation to others and build systems around it?

5|Performance Conversations.trainee_content:
Use the data to manage performance. Ask why before you decide why — don't jump to conclusions.

Hold people accountable and support them at the same time. Change how you say it for each person, but never lower the standard.

Hard feedback done right leaves the BA clear on the problem, owning it, and believing they can fix it.
what_good_looks_like: Opens with data, asks before deciding
Changes tone per person, never changes the standard
BA leaves clear, owning it, and believing they can fix it
how_measured: Watched conversations end with agreed actions
Performance goes up after the talk, relationship stays strong
BAs call the feedback fair, even when it was hard
leader_coaching_notes: Roleplay their hardest conversation that's still pending
Watch one live: does the BA leave with clarity AND belief?
Check they follow through on the agreed actions

assessment_prompts.knowledge: Can you explain how performance conversations work and why they matter at this level?
assessment_prompts.skill: Show me a performance conversation live, with your team watching.
assessment_prompts.consistency: Do you run performance conversations to the standard every week?
assessment_prompts.independence: Can you teach performance conversations to others and build systems around them?

5|Raising the Sector's Average.trainee_content:
Raise the whole sector's average — don't just carry it with your own numbers or one star's.

The middle of the pack is where the power is. Small lifts across everyone beat a hero day from anyone.
what_good_looks_like: Coaches the middle, not just the top and bottom
Sector average climbs over weeks, not just spikes
Everyone improves — check each person's line, not just the total
how_measured: Sector average up across a week, and it holds
